name: Crowley St. Thomas Cargo Terminal - Crown Bay Cargo Port, USVI
type: Marine terminal / container port (smaller, ungated tier)

fieldNotes.siteIdentification: Confirmed against Crowley + Virgin Islands Port Authority (VIPA) sources: this is the Crown Bay Sandfill Marine Cargo Facility on St. Thomas, where Crowley runs its containerized/commercial cargo operation (Crowley Caribbean Services, 8131 Crown Bay, St. Thomas VI 00802). VIPA publishes the facility as ~20 acres with a 2,720 ft bulkhead and 30 ft max draft. Satellite z16-z19 over the Crown Bay waterfront (just west of the Crown Bay cruise pier and the Crown Bay Marina) shows the unmistakable container terminal: dense multi-color container ground slots and stacks, a container vessel worked at the quay, a mobile harbor crane / reach stackers, terminal tractors, and transit-shed warehouses with solar roofs along the landward edge.
fieldNotes.yardSpots: trailerParkingCapacity (~600) is a CONTAINER / CHASSIS GROUND-SLOT estimate, not OTR trailer stalls. Counted from z18-z19 satellite across the Crown Bay cargo yard: several blocks of container ground slots (containers stacked roughly 1-3 high) plus chassis/reefer lanes. This is a small island terminal (~20 acres total, less than a third the size of the Santo Tomas or Puerto Cortes terminals), so slot count is modest by container-port standards. trailersVisible (~25) counts chassis/trailers and discrete container rows discernible in the captured frames. Both flagged uncertain at this resolution.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: 0-10 band, ~4 doors low confidence. This is a marine terminal, so OTR dock doors are near-zero by design; the count reflects the landward face of the attached transit-shed / warehouse buildings where break-bulk and LCL cargo is handled. Imagery shows warehouse roll-up faces but exact door count is not resolvable.
fieldNotes.truckGate: Inferred true: the cargo facility is a fenced, VIPA-controlled port estate (a national port security perimeter) with a single landward access off Crown Bay Road / the Sub Base industrial district. Standard secured-gate configuration for a US territory marine cargo terminal. Specific gate hardware (barrier arm) not resolved in available overhead imagery and no in-terminal Street View exists - flagged uncertain. The named 'smaller, ungated tier' in the pricing refers to the terminal's commercial size class, not a literally open/un-fenced yard; the secured port perimeter is still present.
fieldNotes.guardShack: Inferred true (VIPA-secured federal-territory marine cargo port; ISPS/port-security gate is standard). Specific guard booth not positively resolved in imagery - flagged uncertain. remoteGs left false because a staffed booth is the expected configuration at a manned island cargo gate.
fieldNotes.scale: Inferred true: a weighbridge is standard at a containerized marine cargo terminal for export/import weight verification. Not positively resolved in the captured frames - flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Inferred true: the paved yard between the landward gate and the quay/transit sheds provides interior holding space. Flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.drivewayShort: The landward approach from the public road to the yard is short (1-2 trucks) on this constrained island sandfill site; drivewayLong=false.
fieldNotes.backupSensitive: true: the terminal sits on a tight sandfill peninsula wedged between Crown Bay Road, the marina, and the cruise pier in the dense Sub Base district. A truck queue at the gate has little stacking room and would spill onto the shared public industrial road - tight entry geometry.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Urban: Crown Bay / Sub Base is inside the dense Charlotte Amalie urban fabric of St. Thomas (the island's main commercial port district, surrounded by warehouses, the cruise terminal, retail, and marina). Classified Urban.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: false: a single contiguous cargo estate (quay + container yard + adjoining transit sheds), not a multi-building campus of separate large facilities.
fieldNotes.railServed: false: no rail anywhere on St. Thomas.
fieldNotes.streetView: No Google car coverage inside the secured terminal (metadata ZERO_RESULTS at all in-yard points). Nearest road-level pano is 9NhmCaSc6-JnDE4tOyonfA (captured 2016-10) at 18.33734,-64.95018 on Crown Bay Road ~165m N of the yard, in front of a lumber/hardware store. heading 161 deg points from that pano south toward the terminal centroid. This is an approach view, not the gate itself - perimeter/truckGate streetView coverage is effectively partial.
